terms.gloss: give it here! hand it over! tell me!
evidence: Ter. Ph. 950: Nōlō, volō; volō, nōlō rūrsum; cedo, cape
Traupman 105: out with it! (tell me!), cedo! (pl. cette!)
terms.comment: An old imperative from -ce + the root of dō; it takes an object. Not cēdō, cēdere “go, give way”.

phrases.english: Give me your hands, both of you; we’re crossing the road.

sources: Lewis & Short: cedo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 99, 104.
de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin, s.v. cedo (“give, tell”, imperative).

cedo.claim: short e and short final o, so no macrons
cedo.html: Lewis & Short marks it cĕdo and lists it apart from cēdō, cēdere (“go, give way”); de Vaan s.v. cedo, an imperative (“give, tell”).
